transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I keep losing interest in the projects and activities I usually care about, even when everything in my life is going fine. It's started to cause some real strain with my girlfriend, and after she suggested couples counseling, the intake clinician recommended I get an individual evaluation first.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest, and has it been a single continuous period or have there been separate episodes with times in between when you felt back to normal?

This current low spell where I've lost interest has been hanging around in some form for most of the past year. It’s not just one continuous thing, though—I've been cycling between getting really revved up for a few days and then sinking back into these longer low stretches off and on for about a year now.

During those few days when you feel really revved up, do you also need much less sleep and feel unusually confident, talkative, or impulsive compared with your usual self? Have these periods ever lasted 4 days or more?

Yes, I'll wake up early buzzing with energy without feeling tired, feel like I'm the only one with real vision at work, and impulsively buy things on credit cards. I also get really talkative, even texting old friends late at night about business ideas. These high-energy stretches usually last for a few days at a time, typically around four days or so.

During your low periods, have there been times lasting at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest most of the day nearly every day, along with other symptoms like changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, guilt, or thoughts of death?

Yes, this low spell has been going on for most of the past year, and during it I feel completely dragged down, like I'm walking through mud. I barely eat one real meal a day, my brain is too foggy to concentrate at work, and I feel so guilty about letting everyone down that I've sometimes thought it wouldn't matter if I didn't wake up tomorrow.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent mood episodes over the past year with clear hypomanic periods lasting about 4 days, marked by decreased need for sleep, increased energy, grandiosity, talkativeness, and impulsive spending, along with depressive episodes lasting at least 2 weeks with anhedonia, low mood, reduced appetite, impaired concentration, guilt, and passive thoughts of death. This pattern is most consistent with bipolar II disorder.
